llm.reply:
The tumor suppressor genes BRCA1 DNA repair associated and BRCA2 DNA repair associated are associated with shared and distinct hereditary cancer syndromes as well as constitutional developmental disorders [1][6]. Alterations in these genes confer susceptibility to malignancies including breast, ovarian, pancreatic, and prostate cancers [2][9][11][12]. Bi-allelic germline disruptions also lead to Fanconi anemia complementation groups [5][8].

## BRCA1 Disease Associations
Pathogenic variation in the gene encoding BRCA1 DNA repair associated underlies several hereditary cancer phenotypes [1]. It is implicated in Familial cancer of breast [2]. It confers predisposition to Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 1 [3]. In addition, it is associated with Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 4 [4]. Biallelic mutations result in Fanconi anemia complementation group S [5].

## BRCA2 Disease Associations
The locus for BRCA2 DNA repair associated predisposes individuals to a broad spectrum of familial malignancies [6]. Carriers can develop Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 2 [9]. It is further linked to Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 2 [12]. Affected individuals face risk for Familial prostate cancer [11]. Childhood and central nervous system presentations include Medulloblastoma [7]. It is also connected to Glioma susceptibility 3 [10]. Additional childhood presentations include Wilms tumor 1 [13]. Furthermore, biallelic mutations manifest as Fanconi anemia complementation group D1 [8].

## Biological Context
The product of the BRCA1 locus functions as a tumor suppressor involved in preserving genomic integrity [24: "plays a role in maintaining genomic stability, and it also acts as a tumor suppressor"]. At an epidemiological level, inherited breast and ovarian malignancies are frequently caused by mutations within this locus [24: "Mutations in this gene are responsible for approximately 40% of inherited breast cancers and more than 80% of inherited breast and ovarian cancers"]. Mechanistically, the protein participates directly in double-strand break repair via homologous recombination [21].

The gene NCBIGene:672 is named BRCA1 DNA repair associated [1]. The gene NCBIGene:675 is named BRCA2 DNA repair associated [6]. Gene alterations in these loci confer susceptibility to distinct hereditary malignancies and constitutional disorders [24: "Mutations in this gene are responsible for approximately 40% of inherited breast cancers and more than 80% of inherited breast and ovarian cancers."].

## BRCA1 Disease Associations
The primary condition associated with BRCA1 is Familial cancer of breast [2]. Another associated condition is Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 1 [3]. An additional linked condition is Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 4 [4]. An associated condition is Fanconi anemia complementation group S [5].

## BRCA2 Disease Associations
The locus BRCA2 is associated with Medulloblastoma [7]. Another associated phenotype is Fanconi anemia complementation group D1 [8]. An additional linked condition is Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 2 [9]. A related condition is Glioma susceptibility 3 [10]. Another associated condition is Familial prostate cancer [11]. An additional linked phenotype is Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 2 [12]. The locus is also associated with Wilms tumor 1 [13].

## Molecular Function and Context
The gene symbol is BRCA1 [14]. The gene name is BRCA1 [18]. The gene is annotated with OMIM title BRCA1 DNA REPAIR-ASSOCIATED PROTEIN; BRCA1 [17]. A relevant biological process is double-strand break repair via homologous recombination [21]. An additional process is DNA repair [27]. A related publication title is BRCA1-BARD1 promotes RAD51-mediated homologous DNA pairing. [15]. A linked study is publication pmid: 28976962 [20]. An additional publication title is BRCA1: An Endocrine and Metabolic Regulator. [22]. Another study is publication pmid: 35432218 [26]. A relevant paper title is Preneoplastic stromal cells promote BRCA1-mediated breast tumorigenesis. [28].
